papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable & Environmentally Benign Chemical Science
papers.abstract: Abstract Green chemistry seeks to prevent pollution at its source by reducing waste, energy demand, hazardous substances, and resource consumption. Artificial intelligence (AI), especially machine learning (ML), can strengthen this approach by learning from chemical and process data, predicting outcomes, screening large chemical spaces, and optimizing experiments. Recent literature identifies applications ranging from catalyst discovery and reaction optimization to CO₂ capture, sustainable polymers, waste management, water treatment, and process control. A 2026 review in Applied Intelligence highlights artificial neural networks, random forests, and Bayesian optimization as important approaches across these areas, while also emphasizing data quality, validation, energy use, and scalability as major concerns. (see References 1–6) This project reviews how AI can support the principles of green chemistry and proposes a practical research framework in which sustainability metrics are included directly in model objectives. The central idea is that an AI system should not merely maximize chemical yield; it should seek a balanced outcome involving yield, selectivity, waste, toxicity, energy, solvent impact, and resource efficiency. The report concludes that AI can become an enabling technology for greener chemistry when models are transparent, experimentally validated, and evaluated against environmental as well as technical performance.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modelling of FEA, sampling efficiency, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or any implant/biomechanics application; it is a green-chemistry AI review with no mechanical or biomedical simulation content.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索AI如何支撑绿色化学的源头减污与可持续目标。
summary_zh.method: 综述催化剂发现、反应优化、CO₂捕集等AI应用并提出将可持续指标纳入模型目标的框架。
summary_zh.result: 指出ANN、随机森林与贝叶斯优化是主要方法，但数据质量、验证与可扩展性仍是瓶颈。
summary_zh.validation: 文献综述与概念框架，无实验或数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: To examine how artificial intelligence can reinforce green chemistry principles by reducing waste, energy demand, and hazardous substances at the source.
summary_en.method: A literature review of AI applications in catalyst discovery, reaction optimization, CO2 capture, and process control, combined with a proposed framework that embeds sustainability metrics directly into model objectives.
summary_en.result: Artificial neural networks, random forests, and Bayesian optimization emerge as key approaches, while data quality, validation, energy use, and scalability remain major concerns.
summary_en.validation: No experimental or numerical validation; the work is a conceptual review and research-framework proposal.

summary_en.motivation: Green chemistry aims to prevent pollution at its source, and AI is increasingly proposed to accelerate this goal.
summary_en.method: The work reviews AI and ML applications across catalyst discovery, reaction optimization, CO2 capture, and waste management, and proposes a framework embedding sustainability metrics into model objectives.
summary_en.result: It argues that AI can enable greener chemistry when models are transparent, validated, and evaluated against environmental as well as technical criteria.
summary_en.validation: No experimental or numerical validation; the contribution is a literature review and conceptual framework.
